ask.text: Every value is a temperature anomaly: the difference from the same place's 1951–1980 average for the same months, in °C. It is not a temperature.

Data: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4), 1 200 km Land-Ocean grid, 2° cells, release created 2026-09-08, newest month August 2026. Annual means and 0.1 °C rounding are this app's. NASA does not endorse this app. Answers drawn from these rows are this app's reading of GISS's published data; NASA has not reviewed them and is not responsible for their accuracy.
A weather station's anomaly is spread over every cell within 1 200 km, and over ice-free ocean the value is a sea-surface anomaly (NOAA ERSST v5). A colored cell need not contain a thermometer.
Cells with no estimate are null, not zero. Data covered 82.7 % of Earth's surface in 1880 and 99.2 % in 2025.
2026 is partial: the mean of 8 published months (Jan–Aug), not comparable cell by cell with full years.

globalAnomalyC is GISS's own global mean (GLB.Ts+dSST.csv). north64AnomalyC and south64AnomalyC are this app's area-weighted means of the map's cells with data north of 64° N and south of 64° S, as its Arctic and Antarctic readings show them, not GISS's zonal means. The warmest and coldest cells are this app's too, from the map's cells.
